blocks.title: Units of length
blocks.md: We measure short things in **centimetres** (cm). We measure longer things in **metres** (m). 100 cm make 1 m.

blocks.caption: A pencil of 6 cm.
blocks.alt: A ruler from 0 to 10 with an orange bar of length 6.

blocks.title: Measure
blocks.md: Put the zero of the ruler at one end. Read the number at the other end. Say the unit. For a classroom or a road we use metres.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Start at 0 on the ruler.
- Do not mix cm and m.
- A door is about 2 m high, not 2 cm.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: A ribbon is from 0 to 7 on the ruler. How long is it?
steps: It ends at 7. It is 7 cm.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: A rope is 2 m long. How many cm?

objectives: Add and subtract amounts of FCFA.
reviewNotes: Prices are made up and small; check which coin values are in common use.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Money
blocks.md: In Cameroon we pay in **FCFA**. Coins: 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 500. Notes: 1000, 2000, 5000, 10 000. We add prices to find the cost.

blocks.caption: FCFA coins.
blocks.alt: Four boxes with FCFA coin values 25, 50, 100 and 500.

blocks.title: Change
blocks.md: **Change** is what the seller gives back. Change = money paid − cost. You pay 500 FCFA for something that costs 350 FCFA. 500 − 350 = 150. Change is 150 FCFA.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Write FCFA after the number.
- Add all the prices first.
- Change is paid minus cost, not cost minus paid.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: A pen costs 150 FCFA. A notebook costs 200 FCFA. How much for both?

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: You pay 500 FCFA for bread that costs 350 FCFA. What is your change?

lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Read half past, quarter past and quarter to.
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Parts of an hour
blocks.md: An hour has 60 minutes. **Half past**: the long hand is on 6 (30 minutes). **Quarter past**: long hand on 3 (15 minutes). **Quarter to**: long hand on 9 (45 minutes).

blocks.caption: Half past 9 (9:30).
blocks.alt: A clock face with the short hand between 9 and 10 and the long hand on 6.

blocks.title: Read the clock
blocks.md: Look at the short hand for the hour. Look at the long hand for the minutes. Each number is 5 minutes: 3 is 15 minutes, 6 is 30.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- At half past 4, the short hand is between 4 and 5.
- Quarter to 5 is 4:45.
- Do not mix the hands.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: The long hand is on 6. The short hand is just after 4. What time is it?

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Long hand on 3, short hand just after 7. What time?

Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Flat shapes
blocks.md: A **triangle** has 3 sides and 3 corners. A **square** has 4 equal sides. A **rectangle** has 4 sides: opposite sides are equal. A **circle** is round.

blocks.caption: Four solid shapes (drawn flat).
blocks.alt: A cube, a ball, a cylinder and a cone with labels.

blocks.title: Solid shapes
blocks.md: A **cube** has 6 faces, like a dice. A **ball** (sphere) is round. A **cylinder** is like a tin. A **cone** has a point, like a party hat.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- A square is a special rectangle, but we call it a square.
- A cube is solid, a square is flat.
- A cube has 6 faces, not 4.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: How many corners has a rectangle?

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: A tin of milk is shaped like which solid?
steps: It has two flat round ends.
